topic: Trigonometry (reduction formulae, trig equations & general solutions)
scope_note: This is the Term 1 ATP topic, distinct from 'Trigonometric Functions' (Term 3, graphs — already built as a separate knowledge base) and from 'Trigonometry (sine, cosine and area rules)' (Term 3, application problems — also excluded). Per the 2026 Grade 11 ATP, this topic covers exactly: (1) deriving/using tanθ=sinθ/cosθ and sin²θ+cos²θ=1; (2) deriving/using reduction formulae for sin/cos(90°±θ), sin/cos/tan(180°±θ), sin/cos/tan(360°±θ), sin/cos/tan(−θ); (3) determining values of a variable for which an identity holds (undefined-value questions); (4) determining general solutions of trig equations, including solutions restricted to a specific interval. Taught in Term 1 (completed by end of March), so — unlike the graphs topic — May/June mid-year papers legitimately examine this content, and are included as full evidence here.

archetypes.name: Given a trig ratio (numeric or in terms of a variable) plus a quadrant/domain restriction, determine other ratio(s) without a calculator
archetypes.description: A value or equation fixing one trig ratio is given (e.g. cos62°=k, 3sinθ=2 with cosθ<0, tcos15°=4, a point on the Cartesian plane), along with a sign/quadrant/interval restriction. Learners use a diagram (Cartesian-plane construction with Pythagoras) or the Pythagorean identity to find other ratios, sometimes leaving the answer in terms of the given variable.
command_verbs_used: with the aid of a diagram
without the use of a calculator

marking_pattern.typical_total_marks: 1-5, most commonly 2-3; rises to 4-5 when the answer must be expressed in terms of a variable (t, g) rather than a numeric value, or when a diagram must be constructed from scratch (point-on-Cartesian-plane setups)
typical_breakdown: M1: correct Pythagoras/identity substitution (or set up diagram: x, y, r)
A1: correct sign choice from quadrant
marking_pattern.consensus: Consistent method (diagram + Pythagoras, or square-and-substitute the Pythagorean identity) across all 26 examples. Mark totals vary by sub-part length (1-5 marks) and complexity of the given setup rather than by a genuine disagreement in method.
marking_pattern.notes: Consistent Accuracy (CA) applies heavily within this archetype: an incorrect value found in one sub-part carries forward for full marks in the next as long as method is correct (e.g. Nov 2023 P2 Q5.2.1->5.2.2->5.2.3; Jun 2023 P2 Q4.1.1->4.1.2->4.1.3a; Nov 2022 P2 Q5.3.1->5.3.2->5.3.3). Cognitive level note: 24 of 26 examples are Routine -- working with a variable (t, g) instead of a numeric ratio value does not raise the level, since the underlying technique (diagram + Pythagoras, or the Pythagorean identity) is unchanged and the booklet explicitly allows 'derivation from given information' at Routine. The two Complex exceptions (Nov 2022 Q5.3.3, Jun 2023 Q4.1.3a) genuinely require connecting two different geometric representations (a rotation between two points; a similar-triangle scaling) rather than a single direct read.

archetypes.language_notes: Restriction usually stated as '... and cos θ < 0' or 'for 0° ≤ θ ≤ 180°'. 'Without the use of a calculator' appears in almost every instance — a required instruction, not optional phrasing.

archetypes.name: Simplify a multi-term trigonometric expression to a single ratio/value using reduction formulae, without a calculator
archetypes.description: A compound expression combining several reduction-formula terms (e.g. sin(180°−θ), cos(360°+x), tan(−x)) is given, either with numeric special angles or a general variable, and must be simplified to a single trig ratio, a single fraction, or a numeric value.
command_verbs_used: simplify to a single trigonometric ratio/function

marking_pattern.typical_total_marks: 3-8 (numeric/special-angle versions tend to sit at 3-6 marks; general-variable versions with more reduction steps run 5-8 marks)
typical_breakdown: 1 mark per correctly-applied reduction identity (each quadrant/co-function reduction is its own accuracy mark)
marking_pattern.consensus: Consistent across all 15 examples: marks are awarded per individual reduction step applied, not just for the final answer — 'answer only' does not get full marks.
marking_pattern.notes: Consistent across all 15 examples: marks are awarded per individual reduction step applied, not just for the final answer -- 'answer only' does not get full marks. Cognitive level note: chaining 2-4 standard reduction substitutions is Routine ('well-known procedures', 'few steps') even when six or more marks are on offer -- mark total reflects length, not cognitive demand. The 4 Complex examples (Nov 2021 Q5.3, Nov 2025 Q4.3.1, Jun 2019 Q2.3, KZN Q4.1.1) each require a non-obvious restructuring step: a negative-common-factor trick, spotting sin^2(theta)+cos^2(theta)=1 mid-expression, a square-root restructuring, or (KZN) simply the longest chain of distinct identities seen in the dataset.

archetypes.language_notes: Numeric versions always specify 'without the use of a calculator'. General-variable versions typically end '...to a single trigonometric ratio of x' or similar, specifying the required final form.

archetypes.name: Solve a trigonometric equation for its general solution (or all solutions on a restricted interval)
archetypes.description: A trigonometric equation (often quadratic in sinθ or cosθ, sometimes requiring a co-function identity to combine two different angle expressions first) must be solved, either for the full general solution (θ = ... + k·360°, k ∈ ℤ) or for all values within a stated interval.
command_verbs_used: in how many quadrants will there be solutions

marking_pattern.typical_total_marks: 1-7 (1 mark for a quick quadrant-count sub-part; 3-7 for a full solve)
typical_breakdown: M1: correct standard form / factorisation (or, if scaffolded by a prior 'show that' sub-part, this step is awarded there instead)
A1 per quadrant/solution family (QI, QII, etc.)
final A1 for correct 'k ∈ ℤ' notation on general-solution versions
marking_pattern.consensus: Consistent method (isolate ratio -> reference angle -> apply CAST/quadrant rule -> write general solution) across all 6; 5 of 6 sit at Routine per the booklet's own anchor example for this exact skill, with only the co-function-conversion example (Jun 2022 Q2.3) genuinely Complex.
marking_pattern.notes: Consistent method (isolate ratio -> reference angle -> apply CAST/quadrant rule -> write general solution) across all 6. Cognitive level note: per the booklet's own Grade 11 worked example ('Determine the general solution of 2sin(x-30)+1=0' = Routine), solving a trig equation for its general solution -- including a quadratic-in-sin/cos version reached by factoring, whether scaffolded or not -- is Routine; factoring a quadratic is itself Routine per the booklet's Grade 10 anchor ('Solve for x: x^2-5x=14'). Only Jun 2022 P2 Q2.3 is Complex: it requires converting sin(x+10)=cos(x-30) into a single-ratio equation via a co-function identity -- a genuine switch of representation -- before the routine general-solution procedure can even begin.

archetypes.language_notes: General solution answers are written 'θ = ... + k.360° ; k ∈ ℤ' (SA convention, k∈ℤ stated explicitly and separately mark-worthy). Restricted-interval versions instead list the specific solutions found within the stated domain.

style_profile.typical_sequencing: This question always opens with short 'given a ratio, find another ratio' warm-ups (trigreduction_001), builds through simplification and proof (trigreduction_002/003), through undefined-value sub-parts (trigreduction_004), and closes with the heaviest cognitive-demand item — a general-solution equation (trigreduction_005, Complex Procedures).
style_profile.scaffolding_pattern: Heavy use of 'hence' and CA (Consistent Accuracy) follow-through: later sub-parts routinely depend on an earlier answer (e.g. Nov 2023 Q5.2.1→5.2.2→5.2.3 all build on the same t; Jun 2023 Q4.1.1→4.1.2→4.1.3 build on the same triangle). A 'show that' sub-part is sometimes inserted immediately before a 'hence, determine' sub-part specifically to de-risk the harder step for weaker candidates (Nov 2023 Q5.4.1→5.4.2).
style_profile.notation_conventions: Intervals stated as 'x ∈ [a° ; b°]' or 'a° ≤ x ≤ b°' (semicolon, not comma, inside interval notation — SA/DBE convention). General solutions always close with '; k ∈ ℤ'. Degree symbol (°) is retained throughout, including inside trig function arguments (sin 28°, not sin 28). Reduction-formula memo lines consistently show the identity used as its own tick (e.g. '✓ cos(180°−θ)=−cosθ') rather than folding it silently into the algebra — worth mirroring in generated marking guides.
style_profile.june_papers_note: Confirmed appropriate: this is Term 1 content (completed by end of March), so May/June mid-year exams correctly and consistently test it every year checked (2019, 2022, 2023, plus the KZN 2024 common test) — unlike the Trigonometric Functions (graphs) topic, no pacing anomaly exists here. June papers are treated as full, equal-weight evidence alongside the Nov papers.

cognitive_level_verification: Cognitive levels re-checked directly against standard_setting_booklet_2026_FET.pdf (WCED MNED, Grade 10-12 Prescribed Cognitive Levels table, page 13-14) after initial drafting. This surfaced a real discrepancy: the booklet's own Grade 11 worked example for ROUTINE (Level 2) is 'Determine the general solution of the equation 2sin(x-30)+1=0' -- the same skill as archetype trigreduction_005 -- yet most examples in that archetype had been classified Complex. On review, several archetypes had over-applied 'Complex' wherever a variable (t, g) replaced a number, or a question chained 2-4 standard reduction steps -- neither is a complexity trigger per the booklet's actual criteria (which explicitly allow 'derivation from given information' and 'generally similar to class' work, however parameterised, to remain Routine). Cognitive levels below have been corrected accordingly; only genuine representation-switching, non-obvious routes, or multi-concept integration are now classified Complex.
tier_method: Analyst-assigned (Claude) using difficulty_tier_rules.md v1.2; not published by DBE. Cognitive level per WC MNED 2026 standard (standard_setting_booklet_2026_FET.pdf).
level_review_note: Human-reviewed Sept 2026 by Anne-Marie. Resolution rules applied: (1) insight-spotting alone (noticing a shortcut/identity mid-expression) does NOT change cognitive level, stays Routine; (2) chain-length/execution difficulty stays Routine but justifies Difficult tier; (3) a geometric/cross-point reasoning step (similar triangles, rotating to a second point, connecting one point's ratio to another's coordinates via a shared angle) counts as Complex; (4) an extra genuine technique layered on top of reduction-formula work (e.g. trig values used as exponents, square-root restructuring) counts as Complex. All previously low-confidence tier calls (27 total) were reviewed against these rules and resolved; tier_confidence now high throughout.
